why: I checked every command in both briefs. `npm test` works, since package.json has the test script. The Check 1 and Check 2 one-liners are valid shell and ES-module JavaScript, and the files they read exist. Check 3 breaks. Its JavaScript sits inside a double-quoted shell string, and bash turns `\\s` and `\\b` into `\s` and `\b` before Node sees them. Inside a JavaScript string literal, `'\s'` becomes a plain `s` and `'\b'` becomes a backspace character. So the pattern `'^#{2,}\\s+\`?'+f+'\\b'` reaches the regex as `^#{2,}s+`?name<backspace>`. That can never match a real `## slugify(s)` heading. The command runs but always reports every export as missing and prints FAIL, even on a correct PR. Because of these layered escapes, it does not work as written in this repository.
